guides.name: Get a soy sauce stain out of clothes (fresh or dried)
aliases: spilled soy sauce on my pants
brown sauce stain on my shirt
steps: Scrape off any extra sauce with a spoon or a blunt knife.
Blot the spot with a paper towel. Do not rub it.
Turn the garment inside out and rinse the stain under cold running water.
Pour a little liquid laundry detergent on the stain and rub it in gently with your fingers.
Let it sit about 10 minutes, then rinse with cold water.
Dried or still there? Soak it 15 to 30 minutes in warm water with color-safe bleach.
Rub a laundry stain remover into the spot and let it sit up to 10 minutes.
Wash it in the warmest water the care label allows.
Check the spot before drying. If any stain is left, repeat and wash again.
safety: Test any cleaner on a hidden seam first; some can change the color.
Do not mix color-safe bleach with chlorine bleach.
Never put a stained garment in the dryer; heat can set the stain for good.
stopIf: The label says dry clean only. Take it to a dry cleaner instead.
The color bleeds or changes when you test the cleaner.

guides.name: Clean white canvas or leather sneakers by hand
steps: Take out the laces and soak them in a bowl of warm, soapy water.
Stuff the shoes with crumpled newspaper so they keep their shape.
Brush off loose dirt with a dry, soft brush or an old toothbrush.
Mix warm water with a small amount of dish soap or mild laundry detergent.
Dip the brush in the soapy water and scrub the soles.
Gently brush the canvas or leather tops. Do not scrub hard.
Rinse the brush in clean warm water and wipe the soap off the shoes.
Blot the shoes with a dry towel to soak up the water.
Let shoes and laces air dry at room temperature, out of direct sun.
safety: Do not put sneakers in the washing machine or the dryer; heat can bend them out of shape.
Use only a little soap; too much can stain leather or strip its oils.
Let them dry fully before wearing; it can take 8 hours or more.
stopIf: The shoes are suede. Water can harm suede, so do not wash them this way.
They still look dirty after you repeat the steps; it may be time for a new pair.

guides.name: TV turns on but the screen stays black (safe checks)
aliases: tv turns on but no picture
tv has sound but no picture
steps: Press Home or Menu on the remote. If a menu shows, the screen works.
If nothing happens, point the remote at a phone camera and press Power.
No light on the phone screen? Put fresh batteries in the remote and try again.
Press Input or Source and choose the input your box is plugged into.
Make sure the cable box, streaming stick or game console is turned on.
Unplug each video cable and push it back in firmly, at both ends.
Turn off the TV and the box, then unplug both from the wall.
Wait one full minute, plug them back in, and turn them on.
Still black? Try a different HDMI port on the TV, or a different HDMI cable.
safety: Never open the back of the TV. There is high voltage inside and nothing you can fix.
Unplug by pulling the plug, not the cord, and never with wet hands.
stopIf: You hear strange sounds or smell burning. Unplug it and call for service.
The screen is cracked or the TV was dropped.
There is still no picture from any input or device. The TV needs service.

guides.name: Washing machine is loud or shakes during spin
steps: Stop the cycle and spread the wet laundry evenly around the drum.
Untangle sheets or blankets; tangled bulky items throw the load off balance.
If the drum is packed tight, take some items out so clothes move freely.
Grip the top and rock the washer. All four feet should stay on the floor.
If a corner wobbles, loosen that leg's lock nut, if it has one, and turn the leg.
Once it stops rocking, tighten the lock nuts back against the washer.
New front-loader? Open the door and push the drum. If it feels solid, shipping bolts are still in.
Remove the bolts from the back with the supplied wrench, then plug the holes with the caps.
Run a small load to check that the shaking has stopped.
safety: Slide the washer gently; too much force can damage its feet.
Keep the shipping bolts in case you move the washer later.
stopIf: Squealing or grinding keeps happening even with a light load.
The noise or shaking continues after balancing and leveling.

guides.name: Coffee or red wine spilled on carpet
aliases: dropped my coffee on the rug
steps: Act fast. Blot up the spill with a dry white cloth or white paper towels.
Mix a quarter teaspoon of dish soap into one cup of lukewarm water.
Test it on a hidden bit of carpet first to make sure the color holds.
Dab a little on the stain with a white cloth, edge to center. Do not rub.
Leave it a few minutes, then blot. Repeat while the stain keeps lifting.
If a mark is left, blot with one cup white vinegar mixed into two cups water.
Rinse with a little cold water and blot until dry.
Cover with paper towels, weigh them down with a book, and leave a few hours.
Brush the carpet pile with your hand and let it air dry.
safety: Use hand dish soap only. Laundry or dishwasher detergent can dye or bleach carpet.
Never make the soap mix stronger; leftover soap makes the spot get dirty fast.
Do not soak the carpet. Use small amounts and blot after each rinse.
stopIf: The test spot changes color. Do not use that mix.
The stain will not lift after several tries. Call a carpet cleaner.

guides.name: Smoke alarm chirps every minute
steps: Listen: one short chirp every 30 to 60 seconds means a low battery.
Get a step stool with a handle bar. Never stand on a chair.
Take the alarm off its ceiling bracket, or open its battery door.
Sealed 10-year alarm? Its battery can't be changed. Replace the whole alarm.
Put in a new battery of the type the maker recommends.
Snap the battery in firmly and close the battery door all the way.
Put the alarm back and press the test button. It should sound loudly.
Still chirping? Take the battery out, hold the test button 15 seconds, then put it back.
Check the date on the back. Ten years old or more? Replace the whole alarm.
safety: On an alarm wired into the house, turn off its circuit breaker before taking it off the bracket.
Wired-in alarms have a backup battery too; replace it at least once a year.
stopIf: Three loud beeps and a pause means smoke. Get out and call 911 from outside.
It does not sound when you press test, even with a new battery. Replace the alarm.
It still chirps after a new battery and a reset. Replace the alarm.
A wired-in alarm chirps when another appliance turns on. Have an electrician check it.
